source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Having fairly little measurable effect on how firmly the uterus is actually able to contract once administered","B":"Being considered inappropriate for use in essentially every postpartum client regardless of their individual clinical situation","C":"It has a well-established safety and efficacy profile with relatively few contraindications, making it the standard first-line uterotonic","D":"Having a notably slower onset of action compared with most of the other uterotonic medications typically available"}}
source_row.rationale: Oxytocin is the standard first-line uterotonic medication for postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony, given its well-established safety and efficacy profile with relatively few contraindications compared to other uterotonic agents.
source_row.stem: A nurse anticipates oxytocin as the first-line medication for a client with postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony. This medication is preferred first-line because:
